rationale: Verified by probing 24 candidates in two boots at base_commit e8f2b9ca6, the second with kirk --verbose so every pick rests on an observed assertion rather than inferred kernel source (round 4's failure mode). setitimer01 scores 16 pass / 2 fail with both failures at the SAME assertion, setitimer01.c:124 'Child: killed by SIGALRM': the ITIMER_REAL case passes end to end, while ITIMER_VIRTUAL must kill the child with SIGVTALRM(26) and ITIMER_PROF with SIGPROF(27). All three timers deliver SIGALRM instead. Root cause is one shared closure: create_process_timer_callback (kernel/src/process/process/timer_manager.rs:106-126) hardcodes KernelSignal::new(SIGALRM) at line 111, and PosixTimerManager::new clones that single callback into all three timers at lines 134-138 (alarm_timer, virtual_timer, prof_timer). SIGVTALRM=26 and SIGPROF=27 already exist in process/signal/constants.rs:55-56, and this function has exactly one caller in the whole tree, so the fix is parameterizing the signal per timer - localized, additive, no new subsystem. Everything the test needs already works: setitimer/getitimer both have handlers wired (SYS_SETITIMER=38, SYS_GETITIMER=36 in syscall/arch/x86.rs:221,223), the virtual/prof CPU clocks are real and already tick (update_cpu_time at timer_manager.rs:65-82 advances user/kernel clocks and drives process_expired_timers for both), and the ovalue readback assertions at lines 80-81 already pass for all three timer types. Host baseline is 18/18 pass. Rejected alternatives, all measured: mincore01-04, mlock01, munlock01, splice01/02, tee01, clock_settime01 and remap_file_pages01 have NO dispatch entry in syscall/arch/x86.rs, so they are missing-feature traps like rounds 3 and 4; every socket candidate (accept*, connect*, send*, recv*, setsockopt*, getsockname01, getpeername01) is blocked by the INADDR_ANY bind gap run-OgXQbF already documented; socketpair01 is the known socket.rs EAFNOSUPPORT defect whose owning file was already touched by the committed socket01 fix; creat08/creat09/open10 are all the S_ISGID inheritance gap that committed run-YIMPAV (mkdir02) diagnosed as needing a fix above the fs layer across 6 filesystems; utimes01/utime06 and chdir01/statfs03 all need a MAY_EXEC/ownership permission layer that barely exists (4 check_permission call sites in vfs/path/), which is broad rather than localized; fcntl27 needs F_SETLEASE, prctl10 needs PR_SET_TSC, getcpu01 returns cpuid 123 for a 2-CPU machine - each a genuinely absent feature. statfs03 came back 'broken', exactly the TBROK-in-setup shape the orchestrator warned against, so it was excluded on that evidence.
notes: Probed in two boots with RELEASE=1 SMP=2, default workdir /tmp, so run_vars is empty and phase 4 verifies with no workdir override. all.txt line 1436 is '# setitimer01'; setitimer02 at line 1437 is already enabled and stays untouched. 25 measurements appended to select.cache (24 probe + 1 host). The cache also holds 34 untaken stale-entry candidates observed passing at this exact commit (clock_gettime01, getsockopt02, statfs01/02, statvfs01/02, read03, readv02, write04, pause01/02, rmdir02, realpath01, and more) - each is a one-line pool edit with no kernel change, the cheapest possible future round, and none was consumed here since a stale pool entry teaches nothing about the kernel. To reproduce the assertion-level output, kirk's --verbose is gated behind KIRK_VERBOSE=1 in run_ltp_test.sh:23-25 and is NOT plumbed through the Makefile's --kcmd-args, so it must be forced in the script; I set it temporarily and reverted it, and the worktree is clean apart from .osdk/.
